Description: Infection of susceptible individuals through exposure to contaminated water, resulting in an asymptomatic infection.
Infection of susceptible individuals through exposure to contaminated water, resulting in a symptomatic infection.
Vaccination of susceptible individuals, conferring immunity.
Recovery of asymptomatic individuals, who then move to the recovered (immune) class.
Cholera-induced mortality among asymptomatic individuals, noted to be at a lower rate than for symptomatic cases.
Shedding of hyperinfectious bacteria into the water reservoir by asymptomatic individuals.
Recovery of symptomatic individuals, who then move to the recovered (immune) class.
Shedding of hyperinfectious bacteria into the water reservoir by symptomatic individuals.
Waning of infection-conferred immunity, causing recovered individuals to become susceptible again.
Waning of vaccine-conferred immunity, causing vaccinated individuals to become susceptible again.
Transition of bacteria from the hyperinfectious state to the less infectious state.

Name: β
Description: Rate of 'contact' with reservoir water, representing the maximum infection rate from the environmental reservoir.

Name: γ
Description: Per capita recovery rate from cholera infection. The reciprocal (1/γ) is the duration of infection.

Name: δ
Description: Decay or removal rate of cholera bacteria in the water reservoir. The reciprocal (1/δ) is the cholera life span in water.

Name: ξ
Description: Rate of water contamination by humans shedding V. cholerae into the water reservoir.

Name: κ
Description: Concentration of cholera bacteria that yields a 50% chance of infection (half-saturation constant).

Name: α
Description: Cholera-related death rate, which can differ for symptomatic and asymptomatic individuals.
